newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART LOSE GROUND AFTER DRAW AT BOTTOM CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART LOSE GROUND AFTER DRAW AT BOTTOM CLUB.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart lost vital ground in the tight German league title race when they could only manage a 1-1 draw at bottom club Freiburg on Sunday.

Fourth-placed Stuttgart, who were without Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, struggled to find the net against a team who look doomed to second division football next season after just four wins all season.
The result left Stuttgart six points behind leaders Bayern Munich who stretched their lead at the top with a 3-0 win at Hamburg on Saturday.

Two minutes after going ahead with a spectacular volley from Pole Radoslav Gilewicz in the 64th minute, Stuttgart failed to clear the ball from defence properly and let in Uwe Wassmer for a vital Freiburg equalizer.
"It was a gift for Freiburg," Stuttgart coach Joachim Loew said. "After taking the lead we can't afford to make mistakes like that in defence."
Stuttgart suffered a further setback after the match when they learned that Dutch libero Frank Verlaat may have torn ligaments in his right ankle and could be out for several weeks.
Champions Borussia Dortmund, who warmed up for their midweek European Cup semifinal with Manchester United by beating Bochum 2-0 at home on Saturday, are second, three points behind.
Bayer Leverkusen are a further two points back in third, one point ahead of Stuttgart.
Freiburg's point hardly helped their fate at the bottom of the table. After finishing 11th last year and third in the previous season, the club are still eight points adrift at the bottom.
